lede: The biggest item on your civic radar this week is the San Miguel County Housing Authority's vote Wednesday to shift Pinion Park income eligibility to 80% AMI — a quiet threshold change that decides who actually gets a shot at a deed-restricted unit in this valley. Also Wednesday, the Ecology Commission takes up a draft ordinance that would ban combustion-powered lawn and garden equipment in Town limits, starting with leaf blowers in 2028. The Housing Authority subcommittee meets the same day on the Martin roof-repair exception, and the Mountain Village Design Review Board weighs in Thursday on a conditional-use permit at 332 Adams Ranch Rd.

notable.stake: Vote shifts Pinion Park eligibility to 80% AMI, changing who qualifies for deed-restricted housing.
Draft ordinance would ban gas-powered lawn equipment in Town limits by 2028–2030.
Martin exception request up for decision — deed-restricted unit repair approval on the table.
DRB recommends on conditional-use permit for tent and food truck at 332 Adams Ranch Rd.
